A_target.statement:
Let $n \ge 2 k$ and let $\FF$ be an [[Definition:Intersecting Family|intersecting family]] of $k$-[[Definition:Subset|subsets]] of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$.
Then:
:$\card \FF \le \dbinom {n - 1} {k - 1}$

B_source.statement:
Let $Q$ be a quantity defined for each arrangement $\sigma$ in a finite set $\Sigma$ of arrangements.
If $\map Q \sigma \le B$ for each $\sigma$, then counting incidences over all $\sigma \in \Sigma$ and averaging gives a bound on the total.

substitutions.the family of arrangements averaged over: all cyclic orderings of the ground set
substitutions.the local quantity counted: the number of family members forming an arc in a given cyclic ordering
substitutions.the local bound: at most k arcs of length k can pairwise intersect in one cyclic ordering

derived.the average of the local bound: the global bound on the family size
derived.the double count over arrangements and s: each k-set is an arc in the same number of cyclic orderings

object_map.reformulation: Replace a direct count of the family by an average of local counts over all cyclic arrangements.

validity_conditions: In a fixed cyclic ordering, at most k of the arcs of length k can pairwise intersect, and this is where the condition n at least twice k is used.
Every k-subset is an arc in the same number of cyclic orderings, by symmetry, so the double count is unbiased.
Averaging the uniform local bound over all cyclic orderings converts it into a bound on the size of the family.
proof_plan: Consider all $\paren {n - 1}!$ [[Definition:Cyclic Permutation|cyclic orderings]] $\sigma$ of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$.

In a fixed $\sigma$, call a $k$-set an arc if its elements are consecutive in $\sigma$.
As $n \ge 2 k$ and $\FF$ is intersecting, at most $k$ members of $\FF$ are arcs of $\sigma$.

Double count the pairs $\tuple {A, \sigma}$ with $A \in \FF$ an arc of $\sigma$.
Each $A$ is an arc in exactly $k! \paren {n - k}!$ cyclic orderings.
Hence:
:$\card \FF \cdot k! \paren {n - k}! \le k \paren {n - 1}!$
